title: Growing a $2k Account to $65,662.04 in 30 Days (My Day Trading Strategy)
summary: A full-time momentum day trader teaches his five-step small-cap strategy (scanner-based stock selection, pullback entries, level 2, exit rules, trade logging) around a 30-day small-account challenge, while disclaiming that results are not typical.

assertions.quote: I've been able to grow my account from a starting balance of $2,000 to over $65,000. That's right, in 30 days.

verdicts.note: Audited one-off runs by professionals exist, but they are selected showcases; population studies of day traders find the large majority lose money, so the result does not generalize.

assertions.quote: In order for a stock to go up 400 500% in one day, there has to be an imbalance between supply and demand.
beginner traders end up holding their losers too long and the result is that their average losers do become bigger

verdicts.note: The disposition effect is well documented in retail trading data, but costs and lack of edge explain losses too.

assertions.quote: put real money on the line until you've first proven you can make money trading this strategy in a simulator
If you risk $1 to make $2, you only need to be right 33% of the time in order to break even.
if you're not tracking your trades, you don't have the opportunity to learn from your mistakes
commission free trading really changed the game because it allowed people to jump in and out without paying a fee

verdicts.note: Retail share of volume and trade counts rose sharply after US brokers went to zero commissions in 2019.
Elimination of commissions fuelled a retail participation boom and rise in day trading; retail options volume grew 143-224% from Nov 2019 to Jul 2021 (descriptive, not a causal test).
A strong late-2018 increase in Brazilian day traders is explained in part by retail brokerages zeroing fees for day traders to lure new investors.

After eToro removed commissions on unlevered stock trades in 18 countries in Apr-May 2019, active investors showed no increase in rebalancing in response to returns (Table A4); a narrow test of trading intensity, not of volume or frequency overall, so only weak evidence against.

assertions.quote: My results aren't typical, and there's no guarantee you'll find success whether you trade with me or you learn on your own.
when you trade against the high frequency trading algorithms, trading large caps, you really don't have a good edge

verdicts.note: Retail traders are at a speed and information disadvantage in liquid names, though the same disadvantage applies in small caps where costs are higher.
